tran-quoc-pagoda.body:
Last checked: November 20, 2026. Opening hours change around Tết and holidays, so confirm at the gate.

Trấn Quốc Pagoda is the red tower you see on postcards of West Lake: an eleven-storey stupa on a small island, reached by a short causeway from Thanh Niên Road. It is Hanoi's oldest Buddhist pagoda and still a working place of worship, with monks, daily ceremonies and local families lighting incense.

Most visits take 30 to 45 minutes. The two things that catch people out are the midday closure and the dress code, so read those first.

Quick answer

  • Where: on Kim Ngư islet off Thanh Niên Road, on the eastern side of West Lake, about 3–4 km from the Old Quarter.
  • Hours: roughly 7:30–11:30 and 13:30 to about 18:00. The gate closes over lunch. Hours run longer and crowds are bigger on the 1st and 15th days of the lunar month.
  • Ticket: free. Donation boxes are inside.
  • Dress code: shoulders and knees covered. It is checked at the gate.
  • Best time for photos: early morning for few people, or late afternoon for warm light on the stupa.

Why it matters

The pagoda traces its origins to the 6th century, under Emperor Lý Nam Đế, when it stood on the bank of the Red River. As the river ate into that bank, it was moved in 1615 to Kim Ngư (Golden Fish) islet in West Lake, where it stands today.

What you photograph is a mix of ages. The halls and courtyards are old, and some statues and an inscription date to 1639. The famous red stupa is much newer: it was built in 1998, rises about 15 metres over eleven storeys and is crowned with a lotus. Knowing this helps you frame it honestly, as a living temple rather than a ruin.

What to see

The stupa

Each storey has six arched openings, each holding a statue of Amitabha Buddha. Walk around it once before you take a photo; the side facing the lake is usually quieter.

The Bodhi tree

In the garden stands a Bodhi tree grown from a cutting of the tree at Bodh Gaya in India, where the Buddha is said to have reached enlightenment. It was a gift in 1959 from Indian President Rajendra Prasad, and it is treated as sacred, so do not climb or lean on it for photos.

Halls and courtyard

The main halls hold gilded statues and old steles. Bonsai, rock gardens and stone lanterns fill the courtyards, which make softer, closer backgrounds than the stupa.

Opening hours, ticket and dress code

WhatDetails
Morningabout 7:30–11:30
Afternoonabout 13:30–18:00 (some sources say 18:30)
Lunar 1st and 15thlonger hours, heavy local crowds
Ticketfree; donations welcome
Dresscover shoulders and knees; no shorts, short skirts or tank tops

If you only have shorts, bring a light sarong or long scarf. Speak quietly, do not point your feet at altars, and ask before photographing monks or people praying. Our Hanoi photography etiquette guide covers this in more detail.

How to get there

From the Old Quarter, a Grab car or taxi takes about 10–15 minutes outside rush hour. Ask for "Chùa Trấn Quốc, Thanh Niên". By bike it is an easy flat ride north. There is no boat or back entrance: everyone walks in along the causeway.

Photo tips

  • Morning (7:30–9:00): the fewest people inside the courtyard. Light is soft and the stupa is not yet in harsh sun.
  • Late afternoon: the stupa turns warm red. From Thanh Niên Road and the lake shore, the sun sets behind the pagoda across the water.
  • Lenses: a wide lens fits the whole stupa inside the courtyard; a 70–135 mm lens from the road compresses the stupa against the lake.
  • Avoid: the lunar 1st and 15th if you want empty frames, and arriving at 11:20, when the gate is about to close.

Combine it with

  • West Lake: stay for sunset on Thanh Niên Road, or rent a bike for part of the loop.
  • Quán Thánh Temple: a short walk south along Thanh Niên Road.
  • One Pillar Pagoda: near Ba Đình Square, a few minutes by car.
  • More places to shoot: 15 Hanoi photo spots you can shoot in one day.

Want photos of yourself here?

Photography is priced per hour for up to 2 guests: Basic 30 USD, Premium 60 USD (from 2 hours) and VIP 99 USD (from 2 hours). See Hanoi photoshoot, or send "PHOTO" to @travelframe.vn on Instagram.

FAQ

Is Tran Quoc Pagoda free?

Yes. There is no ticket. Donations are welcome inside.

What are Tran Quoc Pagoda's opening hours?

Roughly 7:30–11:30 and 13:30 to about 18:00, with a closure over lunch. Hours are longer on the 1st and 15th days of the lunar month and can change around holidays.

Is there a dress code?

Yes. Cover your shoulders and knees. Shorts, short skirts and tank tops can be refused at the gate.

How old is Tran Quoc Pagoda?

Its origins go back to the 6th century, and it moved to its current island in 1615. The red stupa itself was built in 1998.

How long should I spend there?

30 to 45 minutes is enough for most visitors. Add an hour if you want sunset on West Lake afterwards.

hoan-kiem-lake.body:
Last checked: November 20, 2026. Ticket prices and walking-street hours change around holidays, so confirm locally.

Hoàn Kiếm Lake is the centre of Hanoi in every sense. The Old Quarter starts at its northern edge, the French Quarter spreads south and east, and almost every first day in the city passes along its shore. It is small, about 12 hectares, so you can walk all the way round in roughly half an hour.

The lake is free and open all the time. What changes is the mood: tai chi, dancing and jogging at dawn, a quieter shore through the day, and on weekend evenings the roads around it close to traffic and fill with families and street performers.

Quick answer

  • Where: central Hanoi, between the Old Quarter and the French Quarter, ringed by Đinh Tiên Hoàng, Lê Thái Tổ and Hàng Khay streets.
  • Cost: the lake is free. Ngọc Sơn Temple, on the island at the north end, costs 50,000 VND for adults.
  • Walking street: from 19:00 on Friday to midnight on Sunday, the roads around the lake close to cars and motorbikes.
  • Best time: 5:30–7:00 for locals exercising and soft light; blue hour for the lit red bridge.
  • How long: 30–40 minutes for a loop, 1–2 hours with the temple and a coffee.

The legend behind the name

Hoàn Kiếm means "Returned Sword". In the 15th century, under Ming occupation, Lê Lợi led the uprising that drove the Ming out, and he became emperor in 1428. Legend says he fought with a magic sword called Thuận Thiên, "Heaven's Will". Boating on the lake after the war, he met a golden turtle that rose from the water and took the sword back to its divine owner. He renamed the lake to mark the moment.

The turtle is not only folklore. Real giant soft-shell turtles lived in the lake, and Ngọc Sơn Temple displays two preserved specimens.

What to see around the lake

Turtle Tower (Tháp Rùa)

The small three-storey tower on its own islet was built between 1884 and 1886 to recall the legend. You cannot visit it, only look at it from the shore, which is how most people photograph it.

The Húc Bridge and Ngọc Sơn Temple

The red wooden bridge at the north end crosses to Ngọc Sơn Temple on Jade Island. Buy the 50,000 VND ticket before you cross. The temple usually opens from about 7:00 to 19:00, with later closing on weekend evenings. We cover it in detail in our Ngọc Sơn Temple guide.

The weekend walking street

Since 2016, the streets around the lake have been pedestrian-only from 19:00 on Friday until midnight on Sunday. Expect folk games, live music, dance groups and snack stalls, plus thick crowds after 20:00. The neighbouring Old Quarter night market runs on the same evenings. During national holidays the city sometimes adds extra nights.

A simple plan

TimeWhat to do
5:30–7:00Walk the east shore and watch tai chi, dancing and joggers.
7:00–8:00Cross The Húc Bridge to Ngọc Sơn Temple when it opens, before tour groups.
8:00–9:00Breakfast or coffee in the Old Quarter; see where to eat.
EveningCome back at blue hour for the lit bridge, or on Friday to Sunday for the walking street.

Photo tips

  • Dawn: the best time for people photos. Locals exercise in groups on the paths; smile and ask before shooting close.
  • Turtle Tower: walk the shore until the tower lines up against trees, not buildings. A 70–135 mm lens fills the frame from the bank.
  • The Húc Bridge: shoot from the shore just after sunset, when the bridge lights come on but the sky still has colour.
  • Crowds: weekday mornings are calm. Weekend evenings are lively but hard for clean frames.

Nearby

  • Hanoi Old Quarter guide, with a walking route and map.
  • St Joseph's Cathedral, five minutes' walk west.
  • Tràng Tiền Street and the Opera House, a short walk south-east.
  • Trấn Quốc Pagoda and West Lake, 10–15 minutes north by car.

Want photos of yourself here?

Photography is priced per hour for up to 2 guests: Basic 30 USD, Premium 60 USD (from 2 hours) and VIP 99 USD (from 2 hours). See Hanoi photoshoot, or send "PHOTO" to @travelframe.vn on Instagram.

FAQ

Is Hoan Kiem Lake free to visit?

Yes. Walking around the lake is free at any time. Only Ngọc Sơn Temple charges a ticket, 50,000 VND for adults.

When is the Hoan Kiem walking street open?

From 19:00 on Friday to midnight on Sunday every week, with extra nights on some national holidays. Cars and motorbikes are not allowed then.

Can you visit Turtle Tower?

No. It stands on a small islet and is not open to the public. You see and photograph it from the shore.

How long does it take to walk around Hoan Kiem Lake?

About 30–40 minutes at an easy pace. Allow longer if you stop at the temple or for photos.

What is the best time to visit?

Early morning, 5:30–7:00, for local life and soft light. Visit on a weekend evening if you want the walking-street atmosphere.

west-lake-hanoi.body:
Last checked: November 20, 2026. Temple and market hours change around Tết and holidays, so confirm locally.

West Lake (Hồ Tây) is Hanoi's largest lake: about 500 hectares of open water a few kilometres north of the Old Quarter. Not to be confused with the West Lake in Hangzhou, China, Hanoi's version is where the city goes to breathe. There are sunsets over open water, a long shoreline road for cycling, old temples on the banks, and cafés and restaurants along Xuân Diệu and Thụy Khuê streets.

Most visitors come for one sunset or one bike ride. If you have half a day, you can do both and add Trấn Quốc Pagoda on the way.

Quick answer

  • Where: Tây Hồ and Ba Đình districts, about 3 km north of Hoàn Kiếm Lake; 10–15 minutes by Grab from the Old Quarter outside rush hour.
  • Size: about 500 hectares, with a shoreline of roughly 15–17 km depending on the route you follow.
  • Cost: free. The main temples are free too.
  • Best time: late afternoon into sunset, from Thanh Niên Road or the shore near Trấn Quốc Pagoda.
  • How long: 1–2 hours for sunset and a short walk; about 1.5 hours to cycle the full loop.

What to do at West Lake

Watch the sunset

The classic spot is Thanh Niên Road, the strip between West Lake and the smaller Trúc Bạch Lake. Stand near the causeway to Trấn Quốc Pagoda and the sun drops behind the pagoda across the water. Arrive 30–40 minutes before sunset to find a good spot.

Cycle the loop

A path follows most of the shoreline. Cycling the full loop takes about 1.5 hours at an easy pace; walking it takes 3–4 hours. You can rent bikes from shops around the lake, or start from the Old Quarter. Electric buggies also run from Trấn Quốc Pagoda past the main temples if you would rather sit.

Temples on the shore

  • Trấn Quốc Pagoda: Hanoi's oldest pagoda, on an islet off Thanh Niên Road. Closed over lunch; see our opening hours and dress code guide.
  • Quán Thánh Temple: at the southern corner by Trúc Bạch Lake. Read our Quán Thánh Temple guide.
  • Phủ Tây Hồ (Tây Hồ Temple): on the northern shore, with altars to Vietnam's mother goddesses. Free, usually open 6:00–19:00 and later on the 1st and 15th of the lunar month, when it gets very busy.

Trúc Bạch Lake

Thanh Niên Road separates West Lake from Trúc Bạch, a smaller, calmer lake with swan pedal boats and lakeside restaurants. It is a good place to sit after sunset.

Quảng Bá flower market

On the eastern side, on the Nghi Tàm dyke, Quảng Bá is a wholesale flower market that runs through the night, roughly from 20:00 to 6:00. It is busiest between 2:00 and 5:00, when traders load bikes and trucks. It is a rare night-time scene, but go by taxi and expect to stay up late or start very early. For a gentler version, our sunrise photo walk combines flower markets with Long Biên Bridge.

Eat and drink

The eastern Xuân Diệu strip is lined with cafés, restaurants and boutique hotels. The southern shore along Thụy Khuê has seafood restaurants.

A half-day plan

TimePlan
14:00Grab from the Old Quarter to the Quán Thánh Temple corner of Thanh Niên Road.
14:30Walk north along Thanh Niên Road to Trấn Quốc Pagoda (it reopens about 13:30).
15:30Rent a bike or take an electric buggy along the eastern shore towards Phủ Tây Hồ.
SunsetBack on Thanh Niên Road for the sun behind the pagoda.
EveningDinner by Trúc Bạch Lake or on Xuân Diệu.

Photo tips

  • Sunset: expose for the sky and let the pagoda go dark; the silhouette reads better than a flat, bright shot.
  • Portraits: on Thanh Niên Road, put the lake behind your subject and shoot with the sun low behind them for a warm rim of light.
  • Blue hour: stay 15–20 minutes after sunset, when the city lights come on across the water.
  • Weather: hazy days soften the sunset colours. Clear days after rain give the strongest skies.

Want photos of yourself at West Lake?

Photography is priced per hour for up to 2 guests: Basic 30 USD, Premium 60 USD (from 2 hours) and VIP 99 USD (from 2 hours). See Hanoi photoshoot, our Spiritual West Lake tour, or send "PHOTO" to @travelframe.vn on Instagram.

FAQ

Is West Lake Hanoi worth visiting?

Yes, especially for a sunset and a break from the Old Quarter. It is open, quieter and has some of the city's best evening light.

How far is West Lake from the Old Quarter?

About 3 km north. A Grab car takes 10–15 minutes outside rush hour.

How long does it take to cycle around West Lake?

About 1.5 hours at an easy pace for the full loop. Walking it takes 3–4 hours.

Where is the best place to watch the sunset?

Thanh Niên Road, near the causeway to Trấn Quốc Pagoda, where the sun sets behind the pagoda across the lake.

Is it the same as West Lake in Hangzhou?

No. Hangzhou's West Lake is in China. Hanoi's West Lake, Hồ Tây, is in the north of Vietnam's capital.
